note_on_thresholds: Raw model scores are uncalibrated sigmoids; the operating threshold is tuned on train only. The production gate in app/services/gnn_risk.py remains 0.8 (policy threshold).

split_method.rng: single random.Random stream, seed 42; first 1920 draws train, next 480 draws test (disjoint, i.i.d. from the same generator)
split_method.graph_leakage: none possible: every transaction is an independent 4-node/3-edge subgraph with no shared nodes or edges; batching merges DISJOINT subgraphs, so no information flows between train and test samples
split_method.caveat: the split is per-transaction i.i.d. — NOT per-sender and NOT temporal. With real data the same sender would appear in both sides and leak sender-level patterns; production evaluation must split by sender/time.

baselines: Same-split comparisons against a linear rule, logistic regression and boosted stumps are in ml/ablation.md (make ablation) — if the GCN does not beat simple baselines, prefer the simple, explainable baseline.
note: SYNTHETIC BENCHMARK — prototype evidence, NOT evidence of production fraud detection. All samples come from train_gnn.py:sample(), whose fraud/normal feature ranges are the same signals the deterministic stand-in (gnn_risk._risk_score) scores, so these metrics primarily measure how well a model can learn THIS generator's separability and may substantially overstate real-world effectiveness. With 2% symmetric label noise and a 1:7 class imbalance the theoretical AUC ceiling for a perfect ranker is ~0.94. The GCN consumes identical vectors on all nodes, so it reduces to an MLP on tabular features — see ml/ablation.md. Replace with labeled production history (sender/time-split) before any real use.
